overall_notes: The slate is reasonably priced at the cited half-point lines with honest shading for cross-book pairing, but every leg carries unconfirmed app lines and several NBA/NHL spots have back-to-back or injury-driven role risk. I would keep most volume- and market-grounded plays and cut the one NBA under where a depleted GSW rotation could still expand a fringe shooter’s minutes despite the drafter’s shade.

votes.reasoning: Henry’s reception profile is consistently low (0–3 targets, 2+ catches in only 3/9) with a clear passing-down role for Hill, and the cited devig is at the exact 1.5 line with appropriate cross-book shading. Trailing script is the main risk, but he has hit 3+ targets only once all season. I would cut if the pick’em line moves to 0.5 or app shows Goblin/Demon pricing.

Brissett’s TD distribution (0–1 in four of his last five) fits a low-total, Henry-heavy game rather than a blowout-only under, and the two-way price at 1.5 is correctly scoped. Correlation with L1 is a slip-build issue, not a leg-quality issue. A higher pick’em line or confirmed shootout total would weaken this.

The devig math is fine, but with Curry, Butler, Porzingis, and Moody out, Richard’s minutes and attempt floor are not stable enough to trust a 1.5 under at only ~60% after shade. One extra look in a 30-minute role clears the number easily. I would keep only if recent games with similar outs show sustained sub-2 attempt rates.

Four straight games without a make and only 4/10 at 2+ support the under despite Edwards/DiVincenzo outs, and the drafter’s argument that volume already stayed low in a thin rotation is plausible. The edge is thin at 56.9% and wide hold. Cut if his 3PA trend above ~4 in the last two injury games.

Logs are a true coin flip at 2.5, but sub-7 average attempts and explicit non-reliance on a blowout benching align with pick’em settlement rules. B2B and variable minutes keep this medium-confidence. A spread collapse into heavy blowout rest risk would lower confidence.

8/10 at 2+ SOG is strong baseload shooting, MTL on a back-to-back is a modest opponent fatigue tailwind, and FanDuel two-way devig at 1.5 is internally consistent even if single-book. Opponent quality or line move to 2.5 would change the view.

7/10 at 3+ with top-line usage and missing wing shooters supports an over at 2.5 without needing a NYR blowout. MTL’s second night is fatigue risk but he is the primary shot funnel. Pairing with L6 is low correlation but same-game stack awareness applies.

7/9 at 2+ SOG including a 5-shot recent game gives a solid floor, and potential chase script as a road dog can add attempts rather than suppress them. VAN back-to-back is workload risk but not spread-bench risk. Confirm app line at 1.5 and watch if UTA jumps to heavy favorite with pullback in volume.
